# Answer: generator-shortcuts v1 — ed860c0a9107

Question: “For this generator, name the strongest plausible shortcut or rival rule that fits the canonical demonstrations. Give an exact input on which it disagrees with the intended rule, how you checked the output, and whether your proposed generator emits such cases.”

## Rival and canonical fit

**Column-major first-visible overlay is the strongest structural rival identified in this review.** It extracts the same equal-sized containers, aligns their bounding boxes, treats zero as transparent, and takes the first visible payload, but visits containers by `(left, top)` instead of `(top, left)`. Thus it changes only the priority rule while preserving the task's object reasoning.

It fits **all 8 canonical labeled records, comprising 4 unique inputs**. The canonical shapes have no different-color local overlap, so these examples cannot distinguish object order. Last-visible, lowest/highest visible color, palette-appearance priority, and numerical first-payload-color container order also fit all eight. First-container-only fits **0/8**; it is a separate generated-lesson shortcut, not a canonical-fitting rival. [Canonical fit and independent definitions](checks/source-review/rival-baseline.json); [final canonical-fit census](checks/lesson-census.summary.json).

“Strongest” is a bounded review judgment, not a ranking over all possible programs. Unlike the already-declared last-visible rival, column-major survived three actual baseline demonstrations and then failed their query.

## Exact reproduced disagreement

Baseline source: v4.0.0, SHA-256 `e1094f19d9fdddc9c645c810cba5949a937c35f47c05df395b479b3a13dde462`. Generate with seed **20000**, difficulty **easy**, samples **0, 1, 2** as demonstrations and **3** as query. Column-major matches every demonstration. Highest-color and palette-appearance priority also survive those three demonstrations.

The query is the following **20×21** grid. Each digit is one cell; coordinates below are zero-based. The complete four-input JSON is retained in [priority-witness-inputs.json](checks/source-review/priority-witness-inputs.json), with the query at `inputs[3]`.

```text
666666666666666666666
609000666666666910096
600000666666666101006
666666666666666666666
666666666666666666666
666666666666666666666
666666666666666666666
666666666666666666666
666666666666666666666
666666666666666666666
666666666666666666666

666666666666666666666
666666666666666666666
666666666666666666666
666666666666666666666
691010666666666666666
601901666666666666666
666666666666666666666
```

Background is 6. The 2×5 container bounding boxes are `(1,1)-(2,5)`, `(1,15)-(2,19)`, and `(17,1)-(18,5)`. At local `(1,2)`, the first container is transparent. Row-major then selects color **1** from the upper-right container; column-major selects **9** from the lower-left container.

Selected-rule output:

```json
[[9,9,0,1,9], [1,1,1,0,1]]
```

Column-major output:

```json
[[9,9,0,1,9], [1,1,9,0,1]]
```

The four inputs were executed through the supported packet wrapper and public `arcpuzzles apply` command. All **4/4** first-visible Python predictions matched Racket. The receipt pins the baseline generator hash above, executed rule hash **`8e6a03efc456`**, and `rule_hash_matches_catalog=true`. This is reference-executed evidence, not a Python-only label claim. [Public Racket receipt](checks/source-review/priority-witness-racket.json), [predictions](checks/source-review/priority-witness-predictions.json), [verification and file hashes](checks/source-review/priority-witness-verification.json).

## Does the proposed generator emit distinguishing cases?

**Yes, constructively on every default even-index sample.** Final v4.1.0 source SHA-256 is `2d7912fe3e21dbe1bc7fb9ecd3c2300aabbbca5d0a7ab5f6d29c74ba79778a18`. Even indexes default to four row-major corner containers and protect two local coordinates:

| Coordinate | Top-left | Top-right | Bottom-left | Bottom-right | Selected output |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `q=(0,0)` | A | B | A | B | A |
| `p=(0,1)` or `(1,0)` | 0 | B | A | B | B |

A and B are distinct. Column-major returns A at `p`; last-visible returns B at `q`. No single global A/B color ranking explains both outputs. Putting `q` first in every container also makes numerical first-payload-color sorting testable. First-container-only returns zero at `p` and is refuted too. The final sampler emits this disagreement class; the retained exact grid above belongs to the baseline and is not claimed to remain byte-identical after the version change.

Every four consecutive default sample indexes contain two such witnesses. Holding out any one pair leaves at least one witness among three demonstrations. The generator declares period 4 and checks all **seven unique rivals** in `lesson_identifiable`; repeated namespace declarations are not additional hypotheses.

Final source-bound public evidence:

| Check | Observed result |
|---|---|
| [Shared lesson census](checks/lesson-census.summary.json) | 300 lessons, 1,200 unique inputs, 0 production ambiguities and 0/1,200 ambiguous query-role rotations |
| [Period enumeration](checks/schedule-census.summary.json) | Seed 0, all four starting residues in easy/medium/hard: 12 lessons, 48 rotations, 21 unique inputs, no ambiguity |
| [Task tests](checks/task-tests/result.json) | 268 passed, 0 failed/errors/skipped; independent geometry/rival mirrors included |
| [Final battery](checks/after-final/checks/ed860c0a9107_after_battery_summary.json) | 12/12 green, no advisory stages |

The exploratory baseline probe used 300 directly generated Python-mirror lessons at seeds 20000–20099 and indexes 0–3; it found 26 column-major production ambiguities and 78 ambiguous rotations. The final shared census uses a different sampler/seed recipe and actual Racket labels. These are separate finite measurements, **not a paired causal estimate of an ambiguity-rate reduction**.

## Limits and the existing audit lead

Explicit `n_containers=2` or `3` remains supported exactly and keeps the first/last conflict, but falls outside the stronger four-container order guarantee. Positions remain restricted to corners; the strongest witnesses keep `q` at the local origin and `p` adjacent. The tests do not establish arbitrary-placement coverage, unique induction against undeclared programs, or downstream model improvement.

The existing `review-ae7bce401b5111fe:v0001` first-container-only finding remains valid evidence about the old source. The new explicit rival, protected `p`, and final census support a **proposed maintainer resolution as repaired for the exact final source**. This return does not automatically close that finding or refresh approval. The first/last parametric prototype remains a separate proposal; its canonical-only negative controls confirm that canonical examples alone cannot select either priority. [Prototype evidence](checks/parametric/final/summary.json).
